extracted.intended_audience: science fiction & fantasy authors, readers, and researchers seeking Nebula Award rules, eligibility, and winner history
extracted.subtask_description: Wikipedia article describing the Nebula Award for Best Novel: its eligibility definitions, nomination and voting procedures, historical rule changes, and list of winners/nominees. Useful for authors checking eligibility and for researchers of award history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a novel (length)
rubrics_metrics.description: A work of fiction is considered a novel by the organization if it is 40,000 words or longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are also given for pieces of shorter lengths in the categories of short story, novelette, and novella. (Verbatim from page: "A work of fiction is considered a novel by the organization if it is 40,000 words or longer; awards are also given out for pieces of shorter lengths, in the categories of short story, novelette, and novella.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — language and place of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Nebula Award consideration, a novel must have been published in English in the US. Works published in English elsewhere in the world are also eligible, provided they are released on either a website or in an electronic edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets both language (English) and distribution conditions (US publication OR online/electronic release if published elsewhere). (Verbatim from page: "To be eligible for Nebula Award consideration, a novel must have been published in English in the US. Works published in English elsewhere in the world are also eligible, provided they are released on either a website or in an electronic edition.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — publication year (post-2009 rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the 2009 awards, nominated works must have been published during that calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaced the earlier rolling eligibility window. (Verbatim from page: "Beginning with the 2009 awards, the rules were changed to the current format, and nominated works must have been published during that calendar year.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — prior (pre-2009) publication-period rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to 2009 the eligibility period for nominations was defined as being one year after the publication date of the work, allowing nomination and awarding in subsequent calendar years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the previous process, works could be nominated in the calendar year after publication and awarded in the calendar year after that; the preliminary list and organizing-panel additions (see separate metric) were part of that older process. (Verbatim summary from page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — expanded works and novellas
rubrics_metrics.description: Novels which were expanded forms of previously published stories are eligible, and novellas published individually can be considered as novels if the author requests it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may request that a novella published individually be treated as a novel for consideration; expanded forms of previously published stories are explicitly eligible. (Verbatim: "Novels which were expanded forms of previously published stories are eligible, and novellas published individually can be considered as novels if the author requests it.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination period and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are nominated each year by SFWA members in a period around December 15 through January 31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The six works receiving the most nominations then form the final ballot, with additional nominees possible in the case of ties. (Verbatim from page: "Works are nominated each year by members in a period around December 15 through January 31, and the six works that receive the most nominations then form the final ballot, with additional nominees possible in the case of ties.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Final ballot voting and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: After the final ballot is formed, SFWA members are given a month to vote on the ballot; final results are presented at the Nebula Awards ceremony in May.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ties in the final vote are broken, if possible, by the number of nominations the works received. Authors are not permitted to nominate their own works. (Verbatim/context from page: "Soon after, members are given a month to vote on the ballot, and the final results are presented at the Nebula Awards ceremony in May. Authors are not permitted to nominate their own works, and ties in the final vote are broken, if possible, by the number of nominations the works received.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Who votes and who may be nominated
rubrics_metrics.description: Nebula Award nominees and winners are chosen by members of SFWA, though the authors nominated do not need to be members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nomination and final selection are member-driven; nominees can be non-members. (Verbatim from page: "Nebula Award nominees and winners are chosen by members of SFWA, though the authors nominated do not need to be members.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-nomination prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not permitted to nominate their own works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit constraint on the nomination process to prevent self-nomination. (Stated on the page as noted under voting/nomination rules.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiebreaking rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Ties in the final vote are broken, if possible, by the number of nominations the works received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If still unresolved, other procedures (not detailed on this page) may apply; the page explicitly notes breaking ties by nomination counts when possible. (Verbatim from page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-2009 preliminary-list threshold and organizing-panel additions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the pre-2009 process, works were added to a preliminary list for the year if they had ten or more nominations; that preliminary list was then voted on to create a final ballot, and the SFWA organizing panel was allowed to add an additional work if they felt it was overlooked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes historical mechanics that differ from the current (post-2009) calendar-year rule and six-work final ballot. (Verbatim/context from page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-year identification convention
rubrics_metrics.description: SFWA currently identifies the awards by the year of publication, i.e., the year prior to the year in which the award is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a labeling/metadata convention used on the page and by SFWA (useful when correlating award year with publication year). (Verbatim/context from page: "SFWA currently identifies the awards by the year of publication, that is, the year prior to the year in which the award is given.")
